content.title: Asian shares sink after losses for Big Tech pull US stocks lower
content.summary: Tokyo’s benchmark Nikkei 225 index tumbled more than 4% on Wednesday and other shares in Asia also sank after a retreat on Wall Street spurred by selling of Big Tech shares.  U.S. futures were slightly lower and oil prices also fell.  Shares in computer chip maker Tokyo Electron dropped 6.1% while stock in Advantest Corp., a maker of semiconductor testing equipment, lost 10%.

content.title: AI Earnings Strength Widens to More Stocks to Allay Bubble Fears
content.summary: SK Hynix Inc. and Advantest Corp. both reported stronger earnings on Wednesday, adding to a slew of results that show demand is rising in tandem with valuations.  Nvidia Corp. extended gains to more than 8.5% in Asia after US President Donald Trump said he would speak with his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping about the company’s Blackwell chip.  The synchronized strength — spanning chip designers, memory suppliers and test-equipment makers — signals that the AI trade, while facing mounting skepticism, is evolving into an industry profit cycle.

content.title: Advantest hikes profit forecast by 25% on AI boost
content.summary: Japan's Advantest on Tuesday hiked its operating profit forecast for the year ending March 2026 by 25% to 374 billion yen ($2.48 billion) as spending on artificial intelligence drives demand for its chip testing equipment. "We have grown confident that the favourable business environment, supported by the ongoing build-out of global AI data centre infrastructure, will continue," CEO Douglas Lefever told an earnings briefing. Operating profit rose 71% to 108.4 billion yen in the July-September quarter compared to a year earlier, with the company raising its mid-term plan financial targets as AI-related investment boosts the industry.

content.title: Japan’s Nikkei Breaks Key 50,000 Level Ahead of Trump Meeting
content.summary: The country’s first female premier, Sanae Takaichi, who has pledged to bolster national security, is set to meet with US President Donald Trump on Tuesday.  “The mere fact that the Nikkei has crossed the 50,000 milestone could be a factor driving the strength in equities,” said Kohei Onishi, senior investment strategist at Mitsubishi UFJ Morgan Stanley Securities Co.  The Nikkei has surged more than 24% this year, outperforming a 15% gain in the S&P 500, as foreign inflows, easing tariff concerns between the US, and optimism for growth under Takaichi have helped spur equity benchmarks to fresh records.

content.title: Japan stocks soar after Takaichi elected as ruling party leader
content.summary:
STORY: Japanese stocks soared Monday after Sanae Takaichi came out on top to lead Japan's ruling party.

That makes her set to become the country's first female prime minister, subject to confirmation by lawmakers.  

The Nikkei surged close to 5% to hit a new record high.

It passed the 48,000-mark for the first time, as analysts broadly welcomed her commitment to economic stimulus. 

Defense contractor Mitsubishi Heavy Industries was among the top movers, jumping around 11% as more military spending is expected under Takaichi.

Tech stocks also surged, with chip gear maker Advantest jumping 14%. 

:: October 4, 2025

The veteran lawmaker won Saturday's run-off vote in the Liberal Democratic Party race.

Upon victory, Takaichi made clear her priority would be to revive demand and the broader market. 

Known to be an advocate of big fiscal spending, she is a devotee of the stimulus policies developed by her late predecessor Shinzo Abe. 

Takaichi has called for tax cuts to cushion the rising cost of living.

And she's criticized the Bank of Japan's decision to raise interest rates, dimming bets rates will be hiked at its meeting at the end of October.

That saw the yen sink, trading at 150 yen against the dollar.

Longer-term Japanese government bonds also fell, on the expectations Takaichi will push for more spending.
